title: Danaus
summary: Shuckford places his coming into Greece a little before Moses visited the children of Israel, and about twenty years before the Exodus.
description: Added from the Shuckford import. Display only. Shuckford’s years are Anno Mundi, or a “years before Christ” figure he is reporting. This chronology never sets a sort, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person’s birth, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Shuckford is display-only).

reign.date: it was A. M. 2494, as I have placed it, which is about twenty years before the Israelites went out of Egypt
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book V, p. 306 (facsimile PDF p. 402)
reign.note: The footnote says Archbishop Usher supposes that the Parian Chronicon was composed A. M. 3741, and that the Marble puts Danaus 1,247 years earlier. The 1,247 is the Marble’s interval as he reports it. A. M. 3741 is entered separately and is not Danaus’s year.

reign.date: “Sethosis, who was called also Aegyptus, as was his brother Armais known by the name of Danaus”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 130; Manetho, ap. Josephus, Against Apion, book 1
reign.note: No reign length is printed for Sethosis. The edition prints the name as Aegyptus (the scan's capital is Æ). Attached also to danaus because this sentence names him. Not merged with Danaus.

reign.date: and( according to Eusebius and good Authors approuing him) reigned fiue yeeres.
reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Book II, Part I, Chapter II, §. VIII, sig. 172b–173a
reign.note: Body intake. A reign length or duration. Not a yeere of the World. year_am stays null. This does not change the sort.
